transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-12
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Cohen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Dr. Asha Patel (Citrine Head of Data & AI), Michael Renn (Procurement), Sara Kim (Legal)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. We also have Luis, our SE, and we know Asha, Michael, Sara are from Citrine, thanks for taking the time. We'll run through the MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pilot pricing and then finish with next steps.

[00:18] Asha: Thanks Maya, hi Luis. Quick note - we've done an initial tech review and want to make sure we don't get surprised on data residency and KMS. We're a biotech, so PHI-ish traces and some GxP-ish controls, so DPA language is important.

[00:32] Michael: From procurement perspective, timeline is tight - we need vendor approval by end of month if possible. We also need final pricing for a 30-day pilot and any add-on fees.

[00:45] Sara: And legal's looking at liability caps, indemnity, audit rights, and retention. We redlined the MSA and DPA and sent them over; there are a few spots we want clarification on.

[01:00] Luis: Great, thanks. I'll try to keep the technical answers concise - re: KMS, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in the Private deployment and Dedicated options, and hosted can integrate with common KMS providers for at-rest encryption. For clarity, the DPA appendix covers encryption-in-transit and at-rest, and we can add explicit language about SSE-C style customer-managed keys if needed.

[01:20] Maya: On the legal items, we reviewed your redlines. There are a few we can't accept verbatim but we can propose alternative language. For example, on liability caps we typically set it at 3x fees for the prior 12 months; we can discuss carve-outs for willful misconduct.

[01:36] Sara: That liability cap is... expected, but we need to see specific carve-outs for IP infringement and data breaches. Also looking for explicit audit log retention and ability to request forensic logs within 30 days.

[01:50] Maya: Understood. We can add clearer SLA appendix language describing log retention, and we have SOC 2 Type II reports we can share. We'll note the forensic log clause as an addendum for the DPA.

[02:05] Asha: On the technical side, latency is not our primary constraint for the pilot, but we care about determinism and KV cache behavior. Can you confirm how Redwood handles KV cache and burst capacity on Dedicated vs Hosted?

[02:20] Luis: Sure - rough explanation: Dedicated gives you pinning to GPU pools, predictable throughput and consistent KV cache residency, so you get better cache hit rates and more deterministic tail latency. Hosted uses dynamic pooling; we do automatic prefix caching and smart routing but in highly spiky loads Dedicated is better. Also we have autoscaling policies and burst capacity for Dedicated for spikes.

[02:43] Michael: So for our pilot, if we start on hosted and then move to dedicated later, what's the migration burden? Any re-certification needed?

[02:52] Luis: Migration is straightforward - same API, model pinning is handled in deployment config. You'll want to run a brief validation to confirm inference metrics, but no model re-training. There might be quantization/profile changes if you pick a different flavor of model, but functionally it's a config change.

[03:10] Sara: Back to DPA: we redlined data residency to require EU-only storage for EU patient data. Is that feasible with hosted?

[03:19] Maya: Hosted can restrict regionally; we have EU regions and can commit to EU-only processing for those tenants. For strict controls we sometimes recommend Private/VPC so you control egress. But we can scope region restrictions in the DPA appendix.

[03:36] Asha: Okay good. One more tech ask - do you offer field-level encryption or tokenization before data leaves our environment? We want to avoid sending raw identifiers where possible.

[03:46] Luis: We don't provide built-in deterministic field-level encryption in the hosted path but we support client-side tokenization patterns. With Private deployments you can run pre-processing inside VPC. We can include a recommended pattern doc with examples.

[04:00] Michael: Pricing question - for the pilot we were asked to provide a 30-day estimate: 50M tokens total, mixed prompt/response ratio, want price per 1K tokens and any minimums.

[04:12] Maya: For the pilot at that volume, we can offer a pilot pricing package - rough numbers: hosted pay-as-you-go rates apply, but we can provide a pilot discount and a capped spend for the 30 days. I'll follow up with a pricing sheet and a modeled estimate based on 50M tokens. Any concerns about overage or throttling?

[04:30] Michael: We need a clear overage policy and max spend cap option; procurement wants a commit structure or a hard cap to avoid surprise invoices.

[04:39] Maya: We can do a capped spend for the pilot and set rate limits per API key to prevent surprises. We'll call that out in the pilot contract.

[04:47] Sara: SLA specifics - uptime commitment and credits. We redlined 99.9% for production, and wanted 99.5 for pilot? Typical. What do you standardly provide?

[04:59] Maya: Our standard SLA for Hosted is 99.9% platform availability; Dedicated can be higher with SLA-backed latency targets depending on commit. Credits are pro-rated service credits. We can put the SLA appendix with definitions (downtime, measurement windows) and propose service credits that scale with severity.

[05:18] Sara: We also need an incident response SLA - time to acknowledge, time to provide initial RCA, and retention of logs for 90 days.

[05:28] Luis: Acknowledgement within 1 hour for Sev1 on Dedicated with our enterprise support; initial RCA delivery within 72 hours and full RCA within 10 business days is our standard, but we can negotiate faster windows for Dedicated agreements. Log retention 90 days is doable for Dedicated or with add-on retention for Hosted.

[05:47] Asha: Can you confirm where audit logs live and whether they can be exported to our SIEM? We want Splunk/Elastic forwarding.

[05:56] Luis: Yes - we support log forwarding via secure syslog/S3 to your SIEM and have tracing hooks. For Private deployments you can set up direct ingestion. We'll include an integration note and sample config.

[06:10] Michael: On data deletion and retention - your DPA language needs to be explicit about retention periods and deletion upon contract termination. We redlined a 30-day deletion window for copies and 180 days for backups, subject to legal holds.

[06:22] Maya: We can accept 30-day deletion for primary copies and 180-day for backups with a legal-hold carve-out. We'll put that in the DPA appendix and add the backup encryption language.

[06:35] Sara: A question on liability - you mentioned 3x fees cap. For data breach carve-outs can we have an exception?

[06:43] Maya: We can discuss a carve-out for gross negligence and willful misconduct. For third-party breaches due to customer misconfiguration we would not accept unlimited liability, but for certain narrow categories we can consider adjusted caps. We'll have legal circulate proposed language.

[06:58] Asha: Anything else about the pilot performance? We want to run a small benchmark: 1k qps bursts, average 100 token generation, measure p90/p99 latency. Can you run that?

[07:10] Luis: Yes - we can run a pilot perf plan. For 1k qps bursts we typically use dedicated pool; hosted might struggle with sustained 1k qps unless it's a large multi-GPU pool. I'll put together a benchmark plan with target metrics and test harness details.

[07:28] Michael: Ok. For procurement approvals, we need a single document that lists all redlines and Redwood's responses. Can you produce a redline tracker?

[07:36] Maya: Absolutely - we'll produce a redline tracker CSV and a short cover note for legal. We'll also include links to SOC2 and the security questionnaire answers.

[07:45] Sara: One last question - are there any subcontractors or subprocessors we should know of? We need a subprocessors list and notification process.

[07:53] Maya: We maintain a subprocessors list and will share the current list; the DPA includes a notification clause when we add materially new subprocessors.

[08:03] Asha: Great. That's mostly what we needed. Michael, any procurement items?

[08:07] Michael: Just timeline - if Redwood can get the redlines and pilot pricing this week, we can try to push internal sign-off next week.

[08:15] Maya: We'll aim to send the redline response, pricing sheet, SLA appendix and SOC2 link by Thursday (2026-06-18). Luis will send the pilot benchmark plan by Tuesday (2026-06-16) and we'll schedule the SE onboarding workshop for the week of 6/22.

[08:29] Sara: Sounds good. Couple small clarifications over chat: legal will follow up on one indemnity clause.

[08:35] Maya: Perfect. We'll follow up in writing and post the artifacts in the shared folder - link: https://redwood.ai/secure/citrine/artifacts (placeholder).

[08:45] Luis: Quick tech note - I'll include sample syslog config and a sample KMS integration guide in the artifact pack.

[08:52] Asha: Thanks everyone.

[08:55] Maya: Ok wrap-up - recap of next steps: Maya to send redline responses + pricing + SLA appendix by 6/18; Luis to send benchmark/test plan by 6/16; Asha to share compliance questionnaire answers by 6/17; Michael to confirm procurement timeline by 6/20. We'll schedule the onboarding workshop for week of 6/22.

[09:12] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache, "V P C" spelled out) and some overlap in talk when multiple attendees respond. Links and references are placeholders.
